[DAY6 20:25:30 - DAY6 20:26:00]
I look toward the big screen. Shure: "Yeah, you can't bring this to the table when you go home." I watch Choiszt open a page, find the sheet music, swipe the tablet, and start tuning the guitar. Shure: "First, sit for two years when you're a kid." Alice: "Is that okay?" Shure: "Hmph, what? Okay, okay." Alice: "Okay." I check that Choiszt is looking at the sheet music while Nicous plays the electronic keyboard. Katrina: "Alright, okay." I turn left and right to study the big screen content, then look back at Choiszt as he continues tuning and begins playing the guitar. Alice: "Does the soldier hit people during renovation?" Male Guest: "Let's have one, let's have one."

[DAY6 20:11:02 - DAY6 20:11:28]
I see Choiszt looking at the sheet music. Lucia: "I think it's not bad." I turn left to look at Jack. "Hey, where is everyone?" I turn right to look at Shure. Lucia: "Want some?" I turn left to the photographer, then right back to Shure as Choiszt starts playing the guitar. The photographer is holding a camera and taking pictures of the girl in the back; I glance right toward the photographer and turn right again. Shure begins to sing—she sings really well. Nicous starts playing the electronic keyboard. I glance left and turn right.

[DAY6 20:22:01 - DAY6 20:22:30]
I swipe the sheet music upward on my tablet a few times. To my left, Choiszt lies on the sofa. I watch Nicous play the electronic keyboard seriously while Shure smiles and plays the guitar. I listen attentively as Katrina sings beautifully.

[DAY6 20:16:01 - DAY6 20:16:30]
I hold the tablet with my left hand and put my right hand in front of it. I look at the sheet music and scroll it upward, sliding it up again, then stop and look at the tablet. I sway to the melody as others listen attentively, and I notice the photographer standing and looking at the sheet music on the large screen. Shure and his girlfriend sing beautifully.

[DAY6 20:30:31 - DAY6 20:31:00]
I watch Choiszt's playing, impressed by their skill. I listen as Jack sings passionately and hits the high notes. Nicous keeps the beat and plays with strong passion. I turn left, glance at the photographer searching for a spot, then turn right. I look at the sheet music on the big screen and notice everyone appreciating the music.

[DAY6 20:30:02 - DAY6 20:30:28]
I sway to the music, turn left then right, and look at the sheet music on the big screen. Katrina also watches the sheet music. Nicous plays the electronic keyboard, tapping the beat with their right foot. Everyone quietly enjoys the music. Jack steps forward to the tablet; Choiszt swipes up on it and resumes playing guitar.

[DAY6 20:36:00 - DAY6 20:39:00]
I observe Jack singing with a microphone in the living room while Violet and Katrina chat nearby. I glance at the sheet music displayed on the big screen, then move toward the back of the living room. Choiszt begins playing guitar, referencing sheet music on a tablet. Katrina engages me in brief conversation as the music continues. Meanwhile, Shure's girlfriend comments on the start of an auction, prompting a discussion among Jack, Lucia, and Alice about ownership and fairness. Jack resumes singing, reading lyrics from his phone, while Alice expresses sleepiness multiple times, which Shure acknowledges. Throughout, I hold and navigate sheet music on my tablet and occasionally glance at the big screen, adjusting my position in the room to follow the music and interactions. This initial phase establishes the setting of a musical gathering with ongoing casual discussions and my active role in managing the sheet music.

I move to the second-floor living room, continuing to focus on the big screen and Nicous, who is near the electronic piano and checking his phone. I use both hands to slide and scroll through the sheet music on my tablet, maintaining attention between the screen and the tablet display. Concurrently, Shure’s girlfriend and Shure discuss various beverages, including sparkling water, rum, and vodka, expressing preferences and regrets over purchases. The photographer takes pictures of Jack singing with his microphone. Alice repeats her tiredness, which Shure suggests she address by sleeping. I persistently scroll through the sheet music while observing Choiszt’s guitar performance, Nicous’s presence, and Jack’s singing. This segment highlights my continued active management of the musical materials while the group engages in light conversation and the atmosphere is documented photographically.

During the musical session, Shure’s girlfriend comments on the style and classification of music, referencing Rosulan and its suitability for cocktails. I reflect on my limited understanding of the genre despite appreciating its taste. The conversation shifts to the categorization of Gongde as rap on NetEase Cloud, sparking debate among Shure, his friend, and others about the accuracy of this classification and the broader definition of rap. I maintain my focus on scrolling through the sheet music on my tablet, resting my hand on the electronic keyboard and intermittently glancing at the big screen and those around me, including Violet and Katrina. I eventually move to sit on the sofa in the living room, continuing to monitor the sheet music and music performance. This event captures the interplay between musical performance, genre discussion, and my continuous engagement with the sheet music and environment.

In the concluding phase, I keep scrolling and swiping through the sheet music on my tablet, closely watching Choiszt’s guitar playing and Jack’s final singing parts. The discussions about music classification continue with Shure and his friend contributing uncertain but animated commentary. I alternate my gaze between the tablet and the big screen, ensuring I follow the musical progression accurately until the performance concludes. This final event summarizes my role in managing the sheet music and observing the musical and conversational dynamics until the end of the session.

[DAY6 20:30:00 - DAY6 20:40:00]
In the dimly lit living room on the second floor, I was engaged in music activities with several others, including Katrina, Choiszt, Nicous, and Jack. I observed the sheet music on the big screen while swaying to the rhythm. Jack was singing with a microphone, Nicous played the keyboard, and Choiszt impressed with his guitar skills. As I looked at the screen, I navigated through the sheet music using a tablet to ensure everyone could follow along smoothly. This setup created a lively and harmonious musical atmosphere.

Jack's singing performance was notable, and I admired his ability to handle high notes, which added to the lively atmosphere. As the song progressed, I continued to interact with the tablet, adjusting the sheet music while occasionally glancing at the big screen. Meanwhile, the photographer captured moments, moving around the room to document the event. Conversations flowed with various participants, including Shure and Katrina, which added to the relaxed ambiance.

Choiszt played the guitar while looking at the music score on his tablet, and Jack continued to sing. I was actively involved in managing the sheet music, ensuring a seamless transition between songs by scrolling through the tablet. The room was filled with a focused energy, as everyone participated in the musical session, either by playing instruments or engaging in light-hearted discussions.

As the performance continued, the room maintained a cozy and vibrant atmosphere. I interacted with the technology at hand, shifting between the tablet and the big screen. Choiszt and Jack's collaboration was well-received, prompting group participation as everyone sang along. The photographer documented the event, capturing the essence of the musical gathering.

Near the end of the session, Choiszt and Jack's performance reached its conclusion. I acknowledged their efforts with applause as the photographer continued to take pictures. The room, filled with various instruments and equipment, was a testament to the collaborative and joyous nature of the gathering. As the event wound down, I continued to ensure the music was organized, looking forward to more musical endeavors.

[DAY6 19:15:00 - DAY6 20:15:00]
Upon arriving in the yard, I observed a photographer capturing images of a boy in a black coat while Shure and his girlfriend posed nearby. I reviewed these photos and provided positive feedback to the photographer. Meanwhile, guests nearby engaged in brief discussions about the photo backgrounds and personal topics. I inquired about a notice posted on the wall to gather context and noted various guests’ activities: Violet was on the phone, Alice was instructing individuals on posing for photos, and Choiszt was playing guitar. Throughout this time, I maintained awareness of the group dynamics and ongoing photo sessions, occasionally interacting with Nicous and Katrina to keep informed about the environment. This initial observation established the setting and identified key participants and their roles in the ongoing event.

I took charge of directing and coordinating the filming process by instructing, “Director, show the director’s cut,” to guide the shoot’s flow. Liu Ting and Alice contributed by prompting specific actions for the subjects. I oversaw technical aspects by observing and responding to questions about AI recognition and lens adjustments, while Jack confirmed that the equipment settings were correct. Moving throughout the set, I addressed critiques, reviewed contacts on my phone to ensure communication lines remained open, and facilitated smooth progression of tasks. Later, I ascended to the living room, where I briefly engaged with Tasha about her activities and participated in light conversation with Alice, Jack, and others before proceeding downstairs. This event reflected my role in managing both creative direction and technical coordination, ensuring that filming and related interactions advanced effectively.

I led the relocation and setup of lighting equipment by first inspecting and unplugging the fill light panel located upstairs. I moved this panel downstairs near the courtyard door and adjusted its position to optimize lighting conditions. Collaborating with Jack, Alice, and others, I discussed color temperature settings and evaluated the light’s effectiveness for the shoot. With Tasha’s assistance, I organized power sockets and managed wiring to maintain safety and accessibility. I then connected the fill light in the yard and coordinated further lighting arrangements with Katrina and Jack, suggesting repositioning to enhance illumination quality. This careful setup supported photography and performance activities by ensuring the environment was suitably lit and technically prepared.

During a photo session focused on Shure and his girlfriend, I observed the posing guided by the boy in the black coat and provided feedback on framing and lighting to improve the images. I facilitated discussions concerning the couple’s relationship status, managing the sharing of information between Shure, Jack, and others to maintain clarity and comfort among participants. As the session concluded, I documented key interactions, noting the completion of the recording and technical issues such as a dead battery. These records ensured that all critical moments and decisions were captured for future reference, maintaining an accurate account of the session’s progress and outcomes.

Inside the house, I managed equipment organization and coordinated with team members by arranging power strips, cables, and lighting panels in the kitchen and living areas. I facilitated necessary setup adjustments as Shure prepared for a performance and engaged in discussions with Nicous, Jack, and Katrina about Shure’s work schedule and financial situation to understand any constraints affecting the event. I monitored group activities, including photographers capturing candid moments and guests enjoying music performances. Additionally, I rearranged seating to create an informal rehearsal atmosphere, concluding this phase with recognition of our collective readiness for upcoming tasks. This event demonstrated my oversight of logistical and interpersonal elements to maintain a conducive environment for performance and social interaction.

While descending the stairway, I held the handrail as Katrina and others debated whether to wait for Tasha’s group or proceed. Upon finding Tasha in the yard corner, I called her over and addressed her hesitation about singing and her missing glasses. After she put on her glasses, I invited her inside and we decided by rock-paper-scissors how I would assist her off a stool, establishing the basis for our collaboration during the event. This interaction highlighted my attentiveness to participant needs and proactive facilitation of inclusive involvement.

Together, Tasha and I ascended the stairs, where I supported her as she nervously descended from the stool. Inside, I gestured for her to lead the way while I closed the door and briefly checked my phone. On the second floor, I coordinated with Shure and Katrina to position a microphone and display lyrics on a large screen. I adjusted equipment settings and confirmed details with the group to prepare for the upcoming singing session, ensuring that both technical and organizational elements were aligned.

Seated and holding my leg, I worked alongside Shure and Choiszt to secure proper sound capture and lyric visibility. I prompted Choiszt to begin speaking as Shure played guitar, while Katrina commented on the setup’s functionality. I actively managed technical and organizational aspects throughout, facilitating smooth communication and coordination during the music activity. This event underscored my role in integrating technical support with group facilitation to enhance performance quality.

The group prepared for a concert in the second-floor living room by arranging seating and coordinating song choices. I observed interactions among Violet, Shure’s girlfriend, and other participants, noting the sheet music displayed on the big screen. Discussions led to agreement to start performances from the beginning of the song, accompanied by mutual encouragement. Meanwhile, the photographer captured images of the setup, documenting the environment and participants’ readiness for live music. This event reflected collective preparation and coordination to initiate the musical segment.

During the live performance, I adjusted the camera angles while watching Shure play guitar and sing. I noted the roles of Jack holding the microphone, Choiszt checking sheet music, and Katrina recording the session on her phone. I danced and clapped as songs ended, demonstrating active participation. Concurrently, Nicous and Jack discussed adding piano accompaniment and song sequencing to enhance the performance flow. This event illustrated my simultaneous engagement in documentation, technical adjustment, and participant interaction to support the musical event’s momentum.

A brief incident occurred near Lucia when an object broke. I intervened by taking the item after confirming it was not glass, thereby allowing activities to continue uninterrupted. Debates over song selection followed, with Katrina and others providing encouragement to maintain participant engagement. This event showed my attentiveness to safety and group dynamics, ensuring the event proceeded smoothly despite minor disruptions.

Earlier in the living room, I moved around swaying to music and interacted with Choiszt using his phone flashlight. After standing and relocating a chair, I observed the lighting conditions, Nicous’s position, and the action camera setup before heading toward the kitchen. There, I checked the big screen and camera configurations, demonstrating active observation and involvement in the gathering’s technical and social elements. This movement reflected my continuous monitoring and adjustment to support event flow.

Throughout the music session, I participated in singing “Unforgettable Tonight” following Shure’s prompt. I observed Nicous and Shure as they debugged sound settings; Nicous unplugged a cable, and Shure took the microphone to perform. I watched their interactions, laughed at technical glitches, and noted Jack’s prompt for emotional preparation before the music commenced. The photographer documented this segment, capturing the event’s unfolding. This event highlighted my multifaceted role in performance participation, technical oversight, and documentation.

On the second floor, I encountered the photographer Tasha, Violet, Alice, and a boy. Sitting on a cushion, I observed Nicous playing keyboard and the big screen displaying song-related content as the group discussed themes like “ego house.” Lighthearted conversations culminated with a guest inviting everyone to sit, reflecting group camaraderie and informal interaction. This event illustrated the blending of artistic discussion and social engagement among participants.

During poetry recitations and performances, I moved within the space, noticing an egg tart and observing Shure’s poetry displayed on the big screen. I laughed at remarks from Katrina, Alice, and Jack and used my phone flashlight during songs to support ongoing activities. I maintained attention on performances by Shure, Nicous, and others, connecting artistic and social segments of the event. This involvement demonstrated my continuous support for creative expression and participant interaction.

The event began with Shure’s humorous comments and poem, which I acknowledged with clapping. I engaged in discussion with Katrina and others about the concept of a “music talk show.” Nicous played keyboard while Jack made jokes about Shure’s condition. I directed attention to the big screen for a group singalong of “Unforgettable Tonight” while answering a call. The group arranged seating, and I recorded the small concert featuring Shure on guitar and Nicous on keyboard, noting the collaborative and lighthearted atmosphere. This event set the tone for the gathering, emphasizing entertainment and group cohesion.

Throughout the musical session, I observed Shure practicing chords and lyrics and supported him by scrolling through lyrics on his tablet. I watched Choiszt join on keyboard and frequently referenced the big screen and tablet to facilitate the performance flow. This support ensured the performers had the necessary technical and organizational resources to maintain continuity and quality.

During group interactions, I monitored discussions about song choices, refreshments, and drinking customs. I noted Alice’s efforts to manage cups and drinks and observed social exchanges among Jack, Alice, Shure, and other participants. The event proceeded with performances by Shure, Choiszt, and Nicous accompanied by continuous photography, highlighting an informal yet coordinated gathering. This event showcased the balance between social management and performance facilitation.

Overall, my role encompassed active observation, technical support with lyrics and sound equipment, facilitating group coordination, participating in singing and poetry recitations, managing equipment logistics, and engaging with participants. These actions ensured a cohesive and smoothly progressing musical and social event, integrating creative expression with effective organization and documentation.
